title: Pontian and Hippolytus (13 August)
hook: a pope and his rival, sent to the same mines, reconciled before dying

segments.voice: Yesterday, Our Lady of the Snows, and a legend of summer snow on a Roman hill. Your line was snow in august. What surprise did you find? Day one thousand fifteen.

Two men on opposite sides of a split in the church at Rome. Each with his own followers. Each sure the other has it wrong. Then the empire arrests them both and ships them to the same place: the mines on the island of Sardinia, where prisoners were sent to hard labor. Same dust. Same chains. Same shortage of food and light. Whatever they argued about in Rome is very far away. Today, a pope and his rival, and what happened to the quarrel underground.
screen: `OPPOSITE SIDES OF A SPLIT.` → `ARRESTED, BOTH OF THEM.` → `THE SAME MINES.`

segments.voice: Hippolytus was a priest and a learned writer in Rome, sharp and serious. He clashed with the popes of his day over teaching and over how gently to treat sinners who wanted to come back. The split went deep enough that a group followed him as their own bishop, against the bishop of Rome. Pontian, later, was that bishop of Rome, the pope. So when the persecution came, the Church in Rome was already divided, and the empire took the two leaders of the two sides. In the mines, tradition says, two things happened. Pontian stepped down from his office, so the Church in Rome could choose a new pope and not be left without a shepherd. And Hippolytus was reconciled to the Church, and urged his followers to return to unity. Both died there, far from home. Their bodies were brought back to Rome, tradition says, and buried, and the Church has kept them together on the same day, the pope and his old rival. Jesus had said it plainly. In the Douay-Rheims: "go first to be reconciled to thy brother." Not after you win the argument. First. These two came to it late, in chains, and the Church still remembers it as peace. The Church didn't remember Hippolytus as the man who split the community. It remembers him, with Pontian, as a martyr who came home. A quarrel that lasted years ended in a mine, and the calendar still sets the two names side by side.
screen: `A PRIEST WHO SPLIT FROM ROME.` · `BOTH SENT TO SARDINIA.` · `ONE STEPS DOWN, ONE COMES BACK.` · `KEPT TOGETHER ON ONE DAY.` · then, large: `GO FIRST TO BE RECONCILED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: bring one rival to mind. Settle, and breathe. Not your worst enemy, just someone you've been on the other side from. A coworker. A relative. An old friend after a falling-out. Picture the two of you somewhere neither of you chose, side by side, with the argument far away. What would you say first? If you pray, you can pray for them by name, and for yourself. If you don't, simply wish them well, once, and mean it as much as you can. The bell holds the time.
Hippolytus, the priest who opposed Pope Pontian's church. Sent to the same mines, the two were reconciled there, and are honored together as martyrs.

Your line: reconciled in the mines. Seven days now: Camillus, Sharbel, James, the house at Bethany, Peter Chrysologus, the summer snow, and now two rivals at peace. Today, if an old quarrel surfaces, don't argue it again. Ask the other person one honest question about how they are. Day one thousand fifteen.

howItsDone: Catholics may keep the optional memorial of Saints Pontian and Hippolytus on 13 August, remembering them together as martyrs.

notes: Hippolytus's dispute is summarized as clashing 'over teaching and over how gently to treat sinners who wanted to come back'; the popes (Zephyrinus, Callistus) are not named. Confirm framing and that Hippolytus is described fairly.
'A group followed him as their own bishop' stands in for 'antipope'; confirm.
Pontian stepping down, Hippolytus reconciling and urging followers back, and the return of their bodies are given as tradition. Confirm.
'Prisoners were sent to work until they broke': description of the Sardinian mines; confirm or soften.
